correctness.rationale: Finite projective-plane axioms q>=2 imply for same-part distinct a,b common/left/right/neither opposite-part incidence counts (1,q,q,q(q-1)), all positive. In 4-round EF game Duplicator matches repetitions, an arbitrarily chosen hidden bipartition alignment, incidence, and for three same-part distinct vertices the common-neighbour predicate. Every 3rd move can preserve that strengthened type: collinear/noncollinear choices both exist. For the 4th move, given three same-side vertices, prescribed nonzero incidence patterns (111 for collinear, 11 pair patterns for noncollinear, singleton patterns both) are available; 000 always supplied by a fresh same-side vertex. For 2+1 split, choices 00/10/01 exist with at most one excluded used vertex; 11 exists precisely if the opposite-side third is not the unique pair join, and either incident/nonincident fresh same-side choices exist. Equalities are preserved. Hence any two planes have the same rank-4 FO theory in pure undirected adjacency, even non-Desarguesian; no named sort or counting. Rank-5 vertex-with-four-distinct-neighbours sentence separates degree-3 Fano Heawood graph from every q>=3. Independent exact EF type recurrence agreed PG(2,2) and PG(2,3) at rank four, corroborating not replacing axiomatic strategy.

evidence: Venema’s 1999 two-sorted modal theorems address a restricted distinct syntax; Pikhurko et al. supply general distinguishing-rank upper bounds.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither entails the positive statement that EVERY two finite projective-plane Levi graphs are rank-four indistinguishable. Even named-side rank-four non-equivalence does not contradict unsorted equivalence.
